feeds.title: Indonesian Teak Furniture Manufacturer: How Golden Village Designs and Builds in Jepara
feeds.lede: Golden Village is an Indonesian teak furniture manufacturer in Jepara, Central Java. We design, kiln-dry, build and hand-finish solid teak furniture for homes, hotels and resorts, and export it worldwide.
feeds.excerpt: Golden Village is an Indonesian teak furniture manufacturer in Jepara, Central Java. We design, kiln-dry, build and hand-finish solid teak furniture for homes, hotels and resorts, and export it worldwide.
feeds.body:
In short: Golden Village is a teak furniture manufacturer based in Jepara, Central Java, the town at the heart of Indonesia’s woodworking tradition. We design our own collections, select and kiln-dry our teak in house, build and hand-finish every piece with local artisans, and ship to private clients, hotels, resorts and trade partners around the world.

Searching for an Indonesian teak furniture manufacturer usually means one of two things: you want furniture made from genuine solid teak, and you want to buy it from the people who actually make it rather than from a reseller. This guide explains what a manufacturer like Golden Village does, why Indonesia leads the world in teak furniture, and what you can expect when you work with us.

What does a teak furniture manufacturer actually do?

A true manufacturer controls the whole chain, from raw timber to a finished, packed piece. At Golden Village that means:

  • Sourcing. We travel widely to find the best sources of teak, build long-term relationships with suppliers, and work with the government forestry department so that trees are regularly replanted.
  • Drying. Every board is kiln-dried in our own chambers, where temperature and moisture are controlled closely. Properly dried teak is stable and far less likely to crack or warp once it reaches your home.
  • Design and prototyping. Our collections reinterpret contemporary European design. Each new piece is drawn, prototyped and refined before it goes into production.
  • Craft. Skilled Jepara artisans, many trained in techniques handed down through generations, shape, join and assemble each piece.
  • Finishing and quality control. Every surface is sanded and finished by hand, then checked before packing.
  • Export. We coordinate international delivery and, where a project needs it, installation.

Why Indonesia leads the world in teak furniture

Teak (Tectona grandis) has been grown in managed plantations on Java for more than a century, which gives Indonesian makers a steady, traceable supply of mature timber. Java also has one of the deepest pools of woodworking skill anywhere, centred on Jepara. That combination of plantation timber, generations of craft knowledge and an export industry built over decades is why so many hotels and furniture brands source from here.

Indonesian timber exports also run through a national legality system, SVLK, which documents where the wood comes from. Our guide on choosing a teak wood furniture supplier explains what to ask for.

European design, Jepara craftsmanship

Golden Village was founded to bring contemporary European design together with the craft traditions of Jepara. You can see it in the collections: the sculpted arms of the Tulipano armchair, the clean trestle base of the Ibiza dining table, and the fluted, wall-hung Rainwood vanity. Each is simple in outline but carefully worked in the details.

Tulipano ArmchairL 81 W 81 H 108Ibiza Dining TableL 180 W 90 H 76Rainwood Bathroom CabinetL 100 W 50 H 30

What we make

Our catalogue runs to more than 300 designs across three collections:

  • Indoor: sofas, lounge chairs, dining tables and chairs, beds, wardrobes, consoles, desks and storage.
  • Outdoor: lounge sets, sun loungers, dining sets and cabanas for terraces, pool decks and resorts.
  • Bathroom: teak vanity cabinets, mirrors, columns and towel racks.

Solid teak is the backbone of almost everything we make, often combined with natural stone, marble, woven cane or upholstery. Anything in the catalogue can be adapted, and our bespoke service builds pieces to your own dimensions and finishes.

Who we work with

Over four decades our furniture has gone into private homes and more than 100 luxury hospitality projects, including Hyatt Makassar, Le Méridien Kuala Lumpur, The Westin London City and resorts from the Maldives to Mexico. We also supply wholesale and trade partners who sell our pieces in their own markets. You can browse the full list on our projects page.

Visit us

You can see the furniture in person at our showrooms in Ubud (Bali), Jakarta, Surabaya and Jepara. The Jepara showroom sits beside the workshop, so it is the best place to see how the furniture is made.

Frequently asked questions

Where is Golden Village based?

Our workshop and showroom are on Jl. Raya Jepara - Kudus KM 13 in Jepara, Central Java, Indonesia. We also have showrooms in Ubud (Bali), Jakarta and Surabaya.

Is Golden Village a manufacturer or a trading company?

We are a manufacturer. We design our collections, kiln-dry our timber in house, and build and finish the furniture with our own artisans in Jepara.

Do you only work with solid teak?

Solid teak is the main material across our collections. Many pieces pair it with natural stone, marble, woven cane, metal or upholstery.

Can you make custom or bespoke furniture?

Yes. We can adapt dimensions, finishes and fabrics on catalogue pieces, or develop new designs from your brief. Our design team prepares material recommendations, pricing and technical drawings.

Do you ship outside Indonesia?

Yes. We export worldwide and have supplied projects across Asia, Europe, the Middle East and the Americas.

feeds.title: Inside a Teak Furniture Factory in Indonesia: From Log to Finished Piece
feeds.lede: How a solid teak chair or table is made in an Indonesian teak furniture factory: log selection, sawing, kiln drying, joinery, hand finishing, quality control and export packing.
feeds.excerpt: How a solid teak chair or table is made in an Indonesian teak furniture factory: log selection, sawing, kiln drying, joinery, hand finishing, quality control and export packing.
feeds.body:
In short: making teak furniture in an Indonesian factory takes nine broad steps: selecting logs, sawing them into boards, kiln-drying the timber, machining the parts, cutting the joints, assembling, hand-sanding and finishing, adding upholstery or stone, and a final quality check before export packing. Drying and finishing take the longest, and they have the biggest effect on how long the piece will last.

Buyers often ask what really happens between a teak log and the chair that arrives at their door. Here is how the process works in a teak furniture factory in Indonesia, with notes on how we approach each stage at our workshop in Jepara.

1. Selecting the logs

Good furniture starts with good timber. Logs are graded by diameter, straightness and how much dense, golden heartwood they contain compared with paler sapwood. Heartwood carries teak’s natural oils, which make it resistant to water, rot and insects, so it goes into the most exposed parts of a piece.

2. Sawing and grading boards

Logs are sawn into planks and graded again. Boards with knots or defects in the wrong place are set aside for hidden parts or smaller components, and the best grain is kept for table tops, arms and anything you see and touch.

3. Kiln drying

Freshly sawn teak holds a lot of water. If it is not dried properly, furniture can crack, warp or open at the joints once it reaches a drier climate or an air-conditioned room. Export furniture is usually dried to a moisture content of roughly 8–12%. We dry all our wood in house, controlling temperature and moisture in the chambers closely. It is one of the most important steps for long-term performance.

4. Machining the components

The dried boards are planed, cut to size and shaped into legs, rails, slats and panels. Curved parts, such as the sculpted frame of a lounge chair, are cut from templates and refined by hand.

5. Joinery

Solid teak furniture relies on proper wood joints, mainly mortise-and-tenon joints and dowels, glued and pinned where needed. Well-cut joinery is what lets a dining chair take years of daily use or a sun lounger survive a resort pool deck.

6. Assembly and hand sanding

Parts are dry-fitted, assembled and then sanded by hand in progressively finer grits. At Golden Village every surface is sanded and finished by hand, which keeps the natural warmth and texture of the wood rather than flattening it under a heavy coating.

7. Finishing

Indoor pieces are finished to bring out the grain and protect against daily wear. Outdoor teak is often left natural so it can weather to a soft silver-grey, or given a finish that slows that change. The right choice depends on where the furniture will live and the look you want.

8. Upholstery, stone and fittings

Many pieces combine teak with other materials: cushions on lounge sets, natural stone basins on bathroom vanities, woven cane panels, marble tops or metal legs. These are fitted and checked at the end of production.

9. Quality control and export packing

Each finished piece is inspected for structure, finish, dimensions and moisture before it is wrapped, protected at the corners and packed for container shipping. Our guide to how an export order works covers what happens after the factory gate.

Want to see it for yourself? Our Jepara showroom sits beside the workshop and is open Monday to Friday.

Frequently asked questions

Why does teak need to be kiln-dried?

Kiln drying brings the timber down to a stable moisture content, usually around 8–12% for export furniture. Without it, teak can shrink, crack or loosen at the joints when it moves to a drier climate or an air-conditioned interior.

What is the difference between teak heartwood and sapwood?

Heartwood is the dense, golden-brown core of the tree and holds the natural oils that make teak durable. Sapwood is the paler outer layer and is less resistant to moisture and insects. Better furniture uses mostly heartwood, especially in exposed parts.

How long does it take to make a teak furniture order?

It depends on the pieces, the quantities and any customisation. We confirm a production schedule with every quotation, and prototypes for bespoke designs are agreed before full production starts.

Can I visit the factory in Jepara?

Yes. Our Jepara showroom is beside the workshop and is open Monday to Friday, 08:00–17:00. Contact us beforehand so the right person can show you around.

feeds.title: Why Jepara? The Town Behind Indonesia’s Finest Teak Furniture
feeds.lede: Jepara, on the north coast of Central Java, has been Indonesia’s woodworking capital for centuries. Here is why so much of the world’s best teak furniture is made there, and how Golden Village fits into that tradition.
feeds.excerpt: Jepara, on the north coast of Central Java, has been Indonesia’s woodworking capital for centuries. Here is why so much of the world’s best teak furniture is made there, and how Golden Village fits into that tradition.
feeds.body:
In short: Jepara is a town on the north coast of Central Java known across Indonesia as Kota Ukir, “the carving city”. It has been a centre of woodcarving and furniture making for centuries, and today thousands of workshops there produce teak furniture for export. Golden Village is a Jepara teak furniture manufacturer: our workshop and showroom are on the Jepara–Kudus road.

A woodworking town with deep roots

Jepara’s reputation for woodcraft goes back centuries. Local tradition credits Queen Kalinyamat, who ruled the coastal kingdom in the 16th century, with encouraging carvers. In the late 19th century Raden Ajeng Kartini, the national heroine born in Jepara, helped bring the town’s carvers to wider attention by promoting their work beyond Java. Over time the skills passed from parent to child, and from workshop to workshop, until furniture making became the backbone of the local economy.

That history matters for one simple reason: skill. Joinery, hand carving and hand finishing are learned over years, not weeks. In Jepara those skills are everywhere, and you can see it in the work.

Close to the teak

Java has managed teak plantations, many of them dating from the colonial era, and Central Java is one of the main growing regions. That puts Jepara workshops close to a steady, traceable supply of mature plantation teak. The port of Tanjung Emas in Semarang is a few hours’ drive away, which makes the town a practical base for exporting by container.

From carving town to design partner

Jepara is famous for ornate carving, but its makers have long since moved beyond it. Many now build clean, contemporary pieces for international brands and hotels. Golden Village was founded on that idea: reinterpret contemporary European design through the craft traditions of Jepara. Our collections are deliberately restrained in outline, and we save the craft for the details: a hand-shaped arm, a perfectly fitted drawer, a top finished by hand.

Sofia ArmchairL 56 W 58 H 80Opera Dining TableL 180 W 90 H 76Maharaja Bed

What to look for in a Jepara teak furniture manufacturer

Jepara has everything from family workshops to large factories, and quality varies. When you compare makers, look for:

  • In-house drying. Ask how the timber is dried and to what moisture content. We kiln-dry all our wood in house.
  • Design capability. Can they develop and prototype new pieces, or only copy existing ones?
  • Finishing standards. Hand finishing makes a visible difference to how a piece feels.
  • Export experience. References from hotels or overseas buyers show they can deliver consistently. Ours are on our projects page.
  • Legal timber. Indonesian wood exports need SVLK legality documents. See our guide on choosing a teak supplier.

Visit Golden Village in Jepara

Our Jepara showroom is at Jl. Raya Jepara – Kudus KM 13, Rengging, Pecangaan, and is open Monday to Friday, 08:00–17:00. If you are in Bali, Jakarta or Surabaya, you can also see the collections at our other showrooms.

Frequently asked questions

Where is Jepara?

Jepara is a town and regency on the north coast of Central Java, Indonesia, roughly 70 km north-east of Semarang, the provincial capital and nearest major port.

What is Jepara furniture known for?

Jepara is known for solid teak furniture and fine woodcarving. Its workshops are known for skilled hand joinery and finishing, and many supply hotels and furniture brands worldwide.

Yes. Our workshop and showroom are on Jl. Raya Jepara - Kudus KM 13, Rengging, Pecangaan, Jepara, Central Java 59462.

Yes. Working directly with the manufacturer gives you control over materials, finishes and customisation. Contact us with your requirements and we will reply within one business day.

feeds.title: How to Choose an Indonesian Teak Wood Furniture Supplier: 10 Questions to Ask
feeds.lede: Ten questions that separate a reliable Indonesian teak wood furniture supplier from the rest: timber grade, legality, drying, joinery, finishing, customisation, samples, packing and references.
feeds.excerpt: Ten questions that separate a reliable Indonesian teak wood furniture supplier from the rest: timber grade, legality, drying, joinery, finishing, customisation, samples, packing and references.
feeds.body:
In short: a good Indonesian teak furniture supplier makes the furniture itself, uses mainly heartwood from documented sources (SVLK), kiln-dries its timber, uses proper wood joinery, finishes by hand, offers samples or prototypes, packs for export, and can show you real projects. Ask about each of these before you place an order.

Indonesia has thousands of furniture suppliers, from one-room workshops to large factories and trading agents. Prices can look similar on paper while the furniture that arrives is very different. These ten questions will help you compare suppliers properly. We have included how Golden Village answers each one.

1. Are you the manufacturer or a trading agent?

Agents can be useful, but you lose direct control over materials and quality. Ask where the workshop is and whether you can visit it. Golden Village: we are the manufacturer, with our workshop and showroom in Jepara.

2. Is it solid teak, and what grade?

“Teak” can mean anything from solid heartwood to veneer over a cheaper core. Ask whether pieces are solid teak and how much heartwood they contain. Heartwood is the dense, golden part of the trunk that carries teak’s natural oils.

3. Where does the timber come from, and is it documented?

Indonesia’s timber legality system, SVLK, verifies that wood comes from legal sources, and wood products exported from Indonesia need SVLK documentation. Since 2016, Indonesian shipments covered by SVLK have been accepted as FLEGT-licensed timber in the European Union. Ask for the documents. Golden Village: we work closely with our timber suppliers and with the government forestry department so that trees are regularly replanted.

4. How is the wood dried?

Poorly dried teak cracks and moves. Ask whether the supplier kiln-dries and to what moisture content (around 8–12% is typical for export). Golden Village: all our wood is kiln-dried in house, in chambers where temperature and moisture are controlled closely.

5. What joinery do you use?

Look for mortise-and-tenon joints and dowels rather than screws and staples alone. Ask to see a joint cut open or a sample piece.

6. How is the furniture finished, and is the finish right for my climate?

Indoor and outdoor pieces need different finishes. A supplier should be able to explain how the finish will behave in a humid tropical villa, a dry air-conditioned hotel or a European winter.

7. Can you customise or build to my design?

Hotels and retailers often need different dimensions, finishes or fabrics. Golden Village: anything in our catalogue can be adapted, and our bespoke service develops new pieces from your brief, with drawings and prototypes.

8. Do you provide samples or prototypes?

For larger orders, approving a sample before production prevents expensive surprises later.

9. How do you check quality and pack for export?

Ask what is inspected (structure, finish, dimensions, moisture) and how pieces are protected for weeks at sea. Our article on how an export order works covers this in detail.

10. Can I see your projects or visit a showroom?

References are the best evidence that a supplier can deliver. Golden Village: our furniture is in more than 100 hospitality projects. See our projects, or visit our showrooms in Ubud, Jakarta, Surabaya and Jepara.

Komodo Dining TableL 210 W 90 H 76Coco Bay SofaL 230 W 100 H 74Karma Cabinet 140L 140 W 50 H 78

Frequently asked questions

What is SVLK?

SVLK is Indonesia’s timber legality and sustainability verification system. It traces wood from its legal source through processing to export, and wood products exported from Indonesia must be covered by it.

Is Indonesian teak as good as Burmese teak?

Old-growth Burmese teak has long been prized, but the EU, the UK and the US now restrict imports of timber from Myanmar. Mature, well-dried plantation teak from Java offers excellent durability with documented, legal sourcing.

How can I tell solid teak from veneer?

Look at the end grain and edges. On solid teak the grain runs continuously around edges and through the thickness, while veneer shows a thin layer over a different core. Ask the supplier to confirm in writing.

Does Golden Village sell to trade buyers and hotels?

Yes. We supply private clients, hotels, resorts, developers, interior designers and wholesale partners. Contact us with your project and we will reply within one business day.

feeds.title: Furniture Exporter from Indonesia: How an Export Order Works, Step by Step
feeds.lede: What happens when you order from an Indonesian furniture exporter: brief and quotation, prototypes, production, inspection, export documents, container loading, shipping terms and delivery.
feeds.excerpt: What happens when you order from an Indonesian furniture exporter: brief and quotation, prototypes, production, inspection, export documents, container loading, shipping terms and delivery.
feeds.body:
In short: an export order from an Indonesian furniture exporter usually moves through seven stages: brief and quotation, samples or prototypes, order confirmation, production, inspection, export documentation and container loading, and finally sea freight and delivery. Agree the shipping terms (Incoterms) at the start so you know who pays for what.

Indonesia is one of the world’s best-known sources of solid wood furniture, and most of it reaches buyers by sea container. If you have not imported furniture before, the process can look complicated. Here is how it works in practice, based on how we handle export orders at Golden Village.

1. Brief and quotation

Start with a clear brief: which pieces, quantities, finishes and fabrics, any changes to dimensions, the delivery destination, and your timeline. The exporter replies with a quotation covering prices, production time and shipping terms. At Golden Village we reply to every inquiry within one business day.

2. Samples and prototypes

For bespoke designs or large orders, a prototype lets you approve proportions, comfort and finish before full production. It is the cheapest point at which to change anything.

3. Order confirmation

Once the quotation and samples are approved, the order is confirmed. Payment terms vary, but a deposit before production with the balance before shipment is common practice.

4. Production

The timber is dried, machined, joined, assembled and finished. Our guide inside a teak furniture factory walks through each step.

5. Inspection

Finished pieces are checked for structure, finish, dimensions and moisture before packing. Many buyers also arrange their own inspection, or an independent one, before the container is loaded.

6. Export documents and container loading

A typical furniture shipment from Indonesia is accompanied by:

  • A commercial invoice and packing list
  • A bill of lading from the shipping line
  • SVLK timber legality documentation (accepted as a FLEGT licence for the EU)
  • A certificate of origin, which may reduce import duty under some trade agreements
  • Fumigation or ISPM 15 treatment for any wooden crates or pallets

Furniture usually ships in 20-foot or 40-foot containers, often 40-foot high-cube for bulky upholstered pieces. Smaller orders can travel as LCL (shared container) freight. From Central Java, containers usually leave through the port of Tanjung Emas in Semarang.

7. Shipping terms (Incoterms)

Term What it means for you
EXW (Ex Works) You collect from the factory and handle everything after that.
FOB (Free On Board) The exporter delivers the loaded container onto the ship at the Indonesian port. You pay sea freight and import costs.
CIF (Cost, Insurance & Freight) The exporter also pays sea freight and insurance to your destination port. You handle import clearance and local delivery.
DDP (Delivered Duty Paid) The exporter delivers to your door with duties paid. This is the simplest option for you, but usually the highest quoted price.

Delivery and installation

For hotel and residential projects, delivery does not end at the port. We coordinate international delivery and white-glove setup where required. Our furniture has gone to projects in the United Kingdom, Spain, Greece, Mexico, Antigua, India, Malaysia, the Maldives, Oman and across Indonesia. See our projects.

Frequently asked questions

Which port do furniture exports from Jepara use?

Most containers from Jepara and the rest of Central Java leave through Tanjung Emas port in Semarang. Some shipments go through Tanjung Perak in Surabaya.

Can I mix different products in one container?

Yes. Mixed containers are common, for example dining chairs, tables and lounge sets loaded together. We plan the loading so the container is used efficiently.

What documents come with a teak furniture shipment from Indonesia?

Usually a commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, SVLK timber legality documentation and, where useful, a certificate of origin. Wooden packing materials are treated to ISPM 15.

Does Golden Village ship worldwide?

Yes. We export worldwide and can coordinate delivery and installation for hotel and residential projects.

How long does sea freight from Indonesia take?

It depends on the destination and route. Within Asia it can be a matter of days to a couple of weeks, while Europe and the Americas typically take several weeks. We confirm the timeline in the quotation.

Tell us what you need. Our team in Jepara replies within one business day.

feeds.title: Teak Furniture Wholesale from Indonesia: A Guide for Retailers, Hotels and Developers
feeds.lede: How to buy teak furniture wholesale from Indonesia: who it suits, how to build a range, customisation, consistency across batches, pricing factors and planning lead times.
feeds.excerpt: How to buy teak furniture wholesale from Indonesia: who it suits, how to build a range, customisation, consistency across batches, pricing factors and planning lead times.
feeds.body:
In short: buying teak furniture wholesale from Indonesia means ordering directly from a manufacturer, by the container or by project, at trade prices. It works best when you plan the range early, agree finishes and fabrics on samples, mix products to fill containers, and allow for both production and sea freight in your timeline.

Who buys teak furniture wholesale?

Most of our trade partners fall into four groups:

  • Retailers and furniture brands who sell Indonesian teak furniture under their own name or ours.
  • Hotels and resorts furnishing rooms, restaurants, lobbies and pool decks. Golden Village has worked on more than 100 hospitality projects, from Radisson Blu Bali to El Fuerte Marbella.
  • Developers and villa operators fitting out several properties to one standard.
  • Interior designers and architects specifying pieces for client projects.

Building a range

Start from the catalogue. Ours has more than 300 designs across indoor, outdoor and bathroom collections. Choosing from one family keeps a project coherent. For example, our Sundara pieces include a bed, desk, buffet, TV unit, lounge chair and an outdoor lounge set, so a villa can be furnished in one design language from bedroom to pool.

Sundara BedL 172 W 221 H 94Sundara Lounge Chair OutdoorL 81 W 85 H 81Savanna Sun BedL 217 W 99 H 36

Customisation

Wholesale orders are often tailored: different dimensions to suit a room plan, a darker or lighter finish, your own fabric on cushions, or a brand-specific detail. Agree changes on a sample or prototype first. Our bespoke team prepares material recommendations, pricing and technical drawings.

Consistency across batches

Teak is a natural material, so colour and grain vary from tree to tree. For repeat orders, and for hotels that add rooms in phases, ask the manufacturer how they keep finish and colour consistent from one batch to the next, and keep an approved sample as the reference.

What affects wholesale pricing?

  • Timber grade and how much heartwood is used
  • Design complexity: curves, hand carving and joinery take time
  • Finishes, fabrics, stone and other materials
  • Order volume and how efficiently it fills a container
  • Shipping terms: an FOB price and a delivered (DDP) price are very different numbers

Planning lead times

Allow for prototyping, production, inspection and sea freight. For hotel openings, work backwards from the opening date and lock the specification early. Our guide on how export orders work covers the shipping side.

Is there a minimum order for wholesale teak furniture?

It depends on the products and the project. Tell us what you need and we will recommend the most efficient way to order, including mixing products in one container.

Can you produce furniture to our own designs?

Yes. We can develop pieces from your brief or drawings, prototype them for approval, and then produce them to your specification.

Is solid teak suitable for commercial hotel use?

Yes. Solid teak with proper joinery is durable enough for heavy daily use in rooms, restaurants and on pool decks, which is why it is widely used in hospitality.

feeds.title: Teak Furniture Q&A: Grades, Durability, Outdoor Use and Care
feeds.lede: Straight answers to the questions we hear most about teak furniture: what Grade A teak means, why teak works outdoors, why it turns silver, how to care for it, and how long it lasts.
feeds.excerpt: Straight answers to the questions we hear most about teak furniture: what Grade A teak means, why teak works outdoors, why it turns silver, how to care for it, and how long it lasts.
feeds.body:
Teak has been used for ship decks, temple doors and fine furniture for centuries, and it is still the timber most people ask us about. Whether you are furnishing a villa terrace in Bali, a hotel pool deck in the Maldives or a dining room in London, the same questions come up again and again: is it really solid, will it survive the weather, why does it change colour, and how do I look after it?

We have answered the most common ones below. The answers come from our own work as an Indonesian teak furniture manufacturer: selecting and kiln-drying timber in Jepara, building and hand-finishing every piece, and seeing how our furniture performs in homes and resorts around the world over the years. If your question is not here, ask us directly.

For a deeper look at the material, see our materials page or our step-by-step guide inside a teak furniture factory.

Frequently asked questions

What is teak?

Teak (Tectona grandis) is a tropical hardwood native to South and Southeast Asia and grown widely in managed plantations on Java, Indonesia. It is valued for its strength, stability, golden colour and the natural oils that protect it from water, rot and insects.

Is teak good for outdoor furniture?

Yes. Teak is one of the best timbers for outdoor use. Its natural oils and silica content help it resist moisture, rot and insects, so solid teak furniture can stay outdoors all year, by the pool or by the sea, without needing a protective coating.

What does "Grade A teak" mean?

Grade A is a trade term for furniture made mostly from heartwood, the mature, golden-brown core of the tree, with little or no paler sapwood. Heartwood holds the most natural oil, so Grade A teak is the most durable and the most even in colour. Lower grades include more sapwood or more variation.

Why does teak turn grey outdoors?

Sunlight and rain gradually change the surface of the wood, turning it from golden brown to a soft silver-grey over a few months. This is purely cosmetic and does not weaken the wood. If you prefer the original colour, clean it and apply a teak protector or sealer regularly.

Should I oil outdoor teak furniture?

It is not necessary. Teak already contains natural oils. Applying oil outdoors can encourage mildew and needs frequent reapplication, so many owners either let the wood silver naturally or use a purpose-made teak sealer to hold the colour.

How do I clean and care for teak furniture?

Wash outdoor teak a few times a year with mild soapy water and a soft brush, working along the grain, then rinse and let it dry. Avoid high-pressure washers, which roughen the surface. For indoor teak, dust regularly, wipe spills promptly and keep it out of constant direct sun and away from heaters.

How long does teak furniture last?

Well-made solid teak furniture with proper joinery can last for decades, both indoors and out. Durability depends on the timber grade, how well it was dried and how it was joined, which is why those are the questions to ask a manufacturer.

Is teak furniture sustainable?

It can be. Plantation teak from Java is grown and harvested in managed cycles, and Indonesian exports are covered by the SVLK legality system. At Golden Village we work with our suppliers and the government forestry department so that trees are regularly replanted.

Can teak be used in bathrooms?

Yes. Teak’s natural oils make it one of the few timbers that cope well with humid bathrooms, which is why it is traditionally used on boats. Our bathroom collection includes teak vanities, mirrors and storage columns.

Why is teak more expensive than other woods?

Teak grows slowly, mature heartwood is limited, and good teak furniture needs careful kiln drying, solid joinery and hand finishing. You are paying for a material and a build that last far longer than cheaper alternatives.

feeds.excerpt: Answers for importers, hotels and designers buying teak furniture from Indonesia: legality, customisation, quotations, shipping, climate, packing and visiting the factory.
feeds.body:
Buying furniture from a manufacturer on the other side of the world is a big step, especially the first time. Most of the importers, hotel groups, developers and interior designers who contact us ask the same practical questions before they commit. How do I know the wood is legal? Can you change a design? How will it travel? Will it survive my climate? Can I come and see it?

Below are our answers, based on how we work with international clients at Golden Village. We are a teak furniture manufacturer and exporter in Jepara, Central Java, with more than 300 catalogue designs, a bespoke service, and furniture in more than 100 hospitality projects across Asia, Europe, the Middle East and the Americas.

For the full process, from quotation to container, read our step-by-step guide to how an export order works. Trade buyers should also see our teak furniture wholesale guide.

Frequently asked questions

Is Indonesia a good place to source teak furniture?

Yes. Indonesia combines managed teak plantations on Java, generations of woodworking skill (especially in Jepara) and a mature export industry. It is one of the world’s leading sources of solid wood furniture for homes and hotels.

How do I know the timber is legal?

Wood products exported from Indonesia must be covered by SVLK, the national timber legality and sustainability verification system. SVLK-covered shipments are accepted as FLEGT-licensed timber in the European Union. Ask your supplier for the documents with every shipment.

Can I change the size, finish or fabric of a catalogue piece?

Yes. Most of our designs can be adapted in dimensions, finish and fabric, and we can build entirely new pieces from your brief. Changes are confirmed on drawings and, where useful, a prototype.

How do I get a quotation?

Send us the pieces you are interested in, quantities, any customisation, your delivery destination and your timeline through our contact page. Our team replies within one business day.

Will teak furniture crack in a dry or cold climate?

Properly kiln-dried teak is very stable, which is why we dry all our wood in house. Like any natural timber it moves slightly with humidity, so keep indoor pieces away from direct heaters and let new furniture acclimatise.

How is the furniture packed for shipping?

Each piece is inspected, then wrapped and protected at the edges and corners for container shipping. Any wooden crates or pallets are treated to the ISPM 15 standard.

Do you supply hotels and resorts?

Yes. Hospitality is a large part of our work. Our furniture is in properties including Hyatt Makassar, Le Méridien Kuala Lumpur, The Westin London City and resorts in the Maldives, Mexico, Spain and India.

Can I visit before ordering?

Yes. You can see our collections at our showrooms in Ubud (Bali), Jakarta, Surabaya and Jepara. The Jepara showroom is beside our workshop and open Monday to Friday, 08:00–17:00.

Do you deliver and install?

We coordinate international delivery and, where a project needs it, white-glove setup on site.

feeds.title: The Outdoor Collection: Designing Teak Furniture for Sun, Salt and Water
feeds.lede: Inside the Golden Village Outdoor Collection: the design thinking behind our teak lounge sets, sun loungers, dining sets and cabanas, and how they are built to live outside all year.
feeds.excerpt: Inside the Golden Village Outdoor Collection: the design thinking behind our teak lounge sets, sun loungers, dining sets and cabanas, and how they are built to live outside all year.
feeds.body:
Outdoor furniture has the hardest job in the house. It sits in full sun, takes tropical downpours, salty sea air and wet swimsuits, and still has to look calm and inviting. Our Outdoor Collection is designed around that reality: solid teak, generous proportions and details that let water drain and air move.

Why solid teak outside

Teak’s natural oils and dense heartwood let it stay outdoors year-round without paint or varnish. Left untreated, it weathers to a soft silver-grey. That patina is part of the look of a mature tropical garden, and it does not weaken the wood. Every outdoor piece we make starts with kiln-dried teak, so it stays stable as it moves between hot sun and humid nights.

Lounge sets: deep seats, open frames

Our lounge sets are built for long afternoons. The Coco Bay sofa pairs a low teak base with rounded rails that wrap the deep cushions. The Sundara outdoor range uses vertical teak slats on its arms and base, a pattern that casts striped shadows and lets rain run straight through. The Lola sofa takes a more classic line, with shaped arms and a simple frame that suits colonial villas and modern terraces alike.

Coco Bay SofaL 230 W 100 H 74Sundara 3 Seaters OutdoorL 231 W 85 H 81Lola 3 SeatersL 185 W 74 H 92

Sun loungers for the pool deck

A good sun lounger has to be comfortable flat and reclined, easy for staff to move, and tough enough for daily resort use. The Savanna sun bed has angled, splayed legs and a thick cushioned platform. The Solea, Levante, Fiore and Orchard loungers range from low, minimal platforms to more structured frames, so a pool deck can mix heights and silhouettes. See the full sunbed collection.

Outdoor dining

The Ibiza dining table stands on angled trestle legs joined by a long stretcher, a structure that stays rigid on uneven terraces. It pairs with the Ibiza armchair and side chair, while the round Palmera and Portofino tables suit smaller courtyards and balconies.

Cabanas: architecture in teak

Our cabanas are the most architectural pieces we make. The Evara cabana raises a cushioned daybed on a stepped teak platform under a slatted pergola roof that filters the midday sun. The Palm Coast cabana offers a wider footprint for beach clubs and large pool decks.

Made for resorts, at home anywhere

Many of these designs were developed with hospitality projects in mind, for resorts such as Fushifaru in the Maldives and Samabe Bali. The same durability makes them just as suited to a private garden. All outdoor pieces can be adapted in size and cushion fabric through our bespoke service.

Frequently asked questions

Can Golden Village outdoor furniture stay outside all year?

Yes. It is made from kiln-dried solid teak, which can stay outdoors year-round. Store or cover the cushions in heavy rain to extend their life.

Will the teak turn grey?

Left untreated, outdoor teak weathers to a silver-grey patina within a few months. If you prefer the golden tone, clean it and apply a teak protector periodically.

Can I choose my own cushion fabric?

Yes. Cushion fabrics and colours can be specified for most outdoor pieces, which is common for hotel and resort projects.

feeds.title: The Indoor Collection: European Lines, Jepara Hands
feeds.lede: How the Golden Village Indoor Collection is designed: living, dining, bedroom and study pieces in solid teak, with contemporary European lines and hand-finished Jepara craftsmanship.
feeds.excerpt: How the Golden Village Indoor Collection is designed: living, dining, bedroom and study pieces in solid teak, with contemporary European lines and hand-finished Jepara craftsmanship.
feeds.body:
The Indoor Collection is the largest part of our catalogue, with well over 200 designs for living rooms, dining rooms, bedrooms and studies. It is also where our founding idea shows most clearly: contemporary European design, made by hand in Jepara. Many families even carry Italian names (Opera, Stanza, San Remo, Dolcevita, Primadonna), a nod to where the design language comes from.

The living room: sculpture you can sit in

Our lounge chairs are where teak becomes sculpture. The Tulipano armchair has a tall, upholstered back held in a single curving teak frame that flows into the arms and legs. The Diane rocking chair balances a deep upholstered seat on long, bent teak runners. For sofas, the Elena, Magenta, Aria and Sundara ranges move from soft and rounded to crisp and tailored.

Tables bring in other natural materials. The kidney-shaped Bulat coffee table floats a stone top above a dark teak shelf, and round tables such as the Tripod, Laguna and Venere add soft curves to a room. Browse lounges and sofas and side and coffee tables.

Tulipano ArmchairL 81 W 81 H 108Diane Rocking ChairL 68 W 100 H 87Bulat Coffee Table Marble TopL 122 W 65 H 43.5

Dining: tables built to gather around

Our dining tables range from the gently curved legs of the Opera to the Komodo, a thick teak top on brushed steel legs, and round tables such as the Venere and Novo. With more than 40 dining chairs to choose from, from the curved-back Sofia to woven and upholstered seats, tables and chairs can be mixed to suit a family kitchen or a hotel restaurant.

The bedroom: calm, complete rooms

Bedroom families are designed as complete rooms: bed, bedside tables, chest of drawers, console, mirror and wardrobe in one language. The Sundara bed wraps an upholstered headboard and base in a slim teak frame. The Maharaja bed builds bedside shelves into a wide headboard with slatted teak wings, a favourite for hotel suites.

Sundara BedL 172 W 221 H 94Maharaja BedStanza Wardrobe 2 DoorsL 120 W 60 H 210

The study and storage

Writing desks such as the Opera and Rosso, bookshelves like the round Saturno, and glass display cabinets in the Milano, Tuscany and Stanza families complete the collection. Each is built in solid teak with proper joinery and drawers that run smoothly for years.

Made your way

Every indoor piece is kiln-dried, assembled and finished by hand in Jepara, and most can be adapted in size, finish and fabric through our bespoke service. To see them in person, visit our showrooms.

Frequently asked questions

How many pieces are in the Indoor Collection?

Well over 200 designs across living room, dining, bedroom and study categories, from sofas and armchairs to beds, wardrobes, desks and display cabinets.

Can I order a matching bedroom set?

Yes. Families such as Stanza, Opera, Dolcevita, Primadonna and Sundara include beds, bedside tables, chests of drawers, consoles, mirrors and wardrobes designed to work together.

Can upholstery fabrics be changed?

Yes. Fabrics and finishes can be specified for most upholstered pieces through our bespoke service.

feeds.title: The Bathroom Collection: Teak Vanities, Stone Basins and Spa-Like Calm
feeds.lede: The design story behind the Golden Village Bathroom Collection: solid teak vanity cabinets with natural stone basins, cane-panelled mirrors, storage columns and towel racks for spa-inspired bathrooms.
feeds.excerpt: The design story behind the Golden Village Bathroom Collection: solid teak vanity cabinets with natural stone basins, cane-panelled mirrors, storage columns and towel racks for spa-inspired bathrooms.
feeds.body:
A bathroom furnished in teak feels closer to a spa than a utility room. Our Bathroom Collection brings warm timber, natural stone and woven textures into the one room where most furniture would struggle, because teak is one of the few woods that genuinely copes with daily humidity.

Why teak works in bathrooms

Teak’s natural oils help it resist water and swelling, which is why it has been used on boat decks for centuries. Kiln-dried and properly joined, a teak vanity handles steam, splashes and humid tropical air far better than painted board or veneer. A gentle wipe after use and good ventilation are all it needs.

Vanity cabinets: three design directions

Our vanity cabinets fall into three broad families.

Slatted and classic. The Karma and Terra cabinets use horizontal teak slats across doors and drawer fronts, a pattern borrowed from tropical shutters. They come in 80 cm and 140 cm widths and are shown with natural stone vessel basins.

Open and airy. The Chakra frames a central bank of drawers between open shelves, keeping towels visible and the piece visually light.

Sculptural and wall-hung. The Rainwood is our most expressive design: a fluted teak drum and a flowing, organic top hung from the wall, with a smooth stone basin resting on top. It comes as a single or double.

Karma Cabinet 140L 140 W 50 H 78Chakra 140L 140 W 50 H 78Rainwood Bathroom CabinetL 100 W 50 H 30

Mirrors with texture

The Aosta mirror sets the glass between two shallow cabinets faced with woven cane, adding hidden storage and a handcrafted texture at eye level. Simpler framed mirrors such as the Bosco and Alpina pair with any vanity. See all bathroom mirrors.

Columns, towel racks and storage

Tall columns such as the Karma, Aosta, Maya and Natura add closed storage in a narrow footprint. The Scala towel rack, a freestanding teak ladder, the compact Tejo rack and a teak laundry box finish the room. See columns and storage.

For homes, villas and hotels

Teak bathroom furniture is a natural fit for villas and resort suites, where guests expect a warm, natural material palette. Widths, finishes and basin choices can be adapted through our bespoke service, and full bathroom sets can be specified for hotel rooms.

Frequently asked questions

Is a teak vanity suitable for a humid bathroom?

Yes. Teak’s natural oils make it resistant to moisture. Wipe away standing water, keep the bathroom ventilated, and a solid teak vanity will last for many years.

What sizes do the vanity cabinets come in?

Sizes range from compact 60 cm single cabinets to 140 cm double vanities, and several models can be made to custom widths.

Are the stone basins included?

Vanities are shown with natural stone vessel basins. Basin and tap options can be confirmed in your quotation.
